app._comment: Static PWA (index.html at repo root, no build step, no root package.json). Served with `python -m http.server 8080` from the repo root; gate.py never starts this itself (checked: nothing in gate.py reads app.start), so the operator running the gate must have that server already up at app.url before running the e2e/a11y_ux domains, or those two will fail closed with connection errors rather than reporting real findings. This local server does NOT apply the repo's `_headers` file (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.) -- those only apply on Cloudflare Pages -- so header-dependent checks here understate what production actually sends. Routes are hash-based SPA routes read from route() in index.html, not guessed: '/' defaults to today's or the latest post; /#/map, /#/ladder, /#/kodex, /#/discover are fixed views; /#/doc/{slug} fetches corpus/{slug}.md (only ai-pr-review and mcp-sensitive-data exist on disk today); /#/2026-07-25 pins a specific day's post and will need updating as the daily post rotates -- it is largely redundant with '/' (same view type) and can be dropped or re-pinned in a later edit without weakening coverage, since '/' already exercises the daily-post view.

unit._waiver_history: WAIVED 2026-07-27 on a WRONG diagnosis, LIFTED 2026-07-29. The waiver claimed the daemon was not running. It was: pid 9784 had held :8788 since 2026-07-22, answering /health 200 and a bare GET 401. The real fault was POST /chat returning 500 from a week-old process whose Claude Agent SDK runtime had gone stale. Restarting it fixed the domain: 10 pass, 0 fail. Two lessons kept here rather than in a commit message. First, 'connection refused' was assumed and never measured; `curl -m 8 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://localhost:8788/health` would have cost nothing. Second, the daemon wrote its stderr nowhere, so the 500 had no trace; it now appends to state/_daemon.log, which is how the restart was confirmed.

Discovery is now scoped by cwd (cd tests), which runs exactly this suite's six files; the tests themselves resolve fixtures via import.meta.url so the cwd change is safe. Runs the whole tests/ directory as of 2026-07-29; it was pinned to tests/boundaries.test.ts back when that was the only file, which meant a new test file would sit in the repo and never gate anything. Measured 2026-07-29: 22 pass, 0 fail, 35 expect() calls across 2 files. tests/mentor.test.ts is pure logic, hermetic, ~60ms: it lifts the המנטור queue block out of index.html and evaluates it, because the app is one inline script with no module boundary and a hand-copied fixture would drift. It carries a regression oracle for the suppression bug found the same day (a belief is keyed semantically, so suppression must match belief.from, not the belief id; proven to fail against the previous logic before the fix). tests/boundaries.test.ts is NOT hermetic and the gate must not be read as if it were: it makes an authenticated, state-mutating (self-restoring) round trip against the LIVE production Cloudflare Worker at https://sadna-sync.shovalb9.workers.dev, and 4 of its 10 tests require a local daemon answering on http://localhost:8788 (started separately via `cd daemon && bun run server.ts`). If that daemon is not running when the gate executes, those 4 fail closed with connection-refused rather than being skipped. COVERAGE BOUNDARY: this domain is example-based and integration only. There is no property-based, mutation, fuzz or contract testing anywhere in this repo, and the gate has no domain for any of them; filed 2026-07-29 to claude-setup as a gap against work-docs/testing_practices.txt section 6.

types._comment:
No tsconfig, .eslintrc, or biome.json anywhere in the repo outside daemon/'s node_modules dependencies, so there is no real typecheck or lint to run -- this is a syntax-only sweep of every piece of JS/shell in the deployed app: sw.js (the only standalone JS file since tree3d.js was deleted on 2026-08-07 as dead code; `node --check tree3d.js` was in this command and failed on node 18 with SyntaxError on `export`, because the file was an ES module and node checks a .js as CommonJS, so the dead file was breaking a required domain), the ~137KB inline <script> block in index.html (the bulk of the app's logic, extracted and checked by the new tools/check_inline_js.py helper added alongside this contract -- see that file for the extraction method), every tools/*.py file via compileall, and the one shell tool script. It catches parse errors, nothing semantic. Personally run 2026-07-25 via the exact shell (subprocess.run(..., shell=True) on Windows, i.e. cmd.exe) that gate.py itself uses: exit 0, 'inline script #0 (113134 bytes): ok' plus clean compileall and bash -n.

EXTENDED 2026-08-10 with tools/check_callsites.py, because everything above this line is a PARSE check and there is a whole defect class it cannot see. A cut that removes a function's last call site leaves syntactically valid JS, so `node --check` exits 0 and check_inline_js.py prints ok; the container is markup so a DOM assertion still finds it; and the feature silently stops rendering. Measured against this repo's own history rather than argued: 8a917e3 orphaned counters() in writing/the-bench.html (3 references before, 0 after, definition untouched) and it stayed broken through 2008446 until e79d5b4 restored the two calls, which is the entire window in which the operator was asked to review that page. `check_callsites.py --base 8a917e3^ --head 8a917e3` exits 1 on that pair and `--base 2008446 --head e79d5b4` exits 0, both run 2026-08-10. The check is delta-based on purpose: an absolute 'every function needs a caller' rule would go red on genuinely dead code mid-removal and on a definition added before its caller, and --selftest asserts both of those false-positive shapes stay green alongside the planted red case. It grades the working tree against HEAD, or HEAD~1..HEAD when the tree is clean, since the gate runs after the final commit and a clean-tree diff would otherwise be green by construction. Exit 2 means it could not measure (no git, unreadable ref) rather than that it failed, per this file's own convention. Also added to .github/workflows/ci.yml, which needs fetch-depth 2 for HEAD~1 to exist.

EXTENDED 2026-08-24 with `cd game && bun x tsc --noEmit`: ADR-0002 commits the game to TypeScript strict, and PR #8's review correctly called the commitment unenforced. game/tsconfig.json carries strict+noEmit; this cmd is the local enforcement. The CI copy rides the migration PR, since ci.yml gains its Bun toolchain there anyway; until then a type error fails the gate, not the workflow.
